requirements.text: The system MUST ingest Markdown source content from a user-specified local directory and include all files with the ".md" extension by default.
requirements.rationale: The project assumes notes are individual Markdown files in a directory and the primary goal is to ingest a collection of Markdown notes.

requirements.text: The system MUST generate a static build output consisting only of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and other static assets (e.g., images) with no server-side runtime dependency.
requirements.rationale: A core constraint and goal is output that can be hosted on common static hosting without requiring a server or database at runtime.

requirements.text: The system MUST render each input Markdown note into a corresponding HTML page in the generated site output, excluding any files explicitly ignored by configuration.
requirements.rationale: Success metrics require all Markdown files be rendered into accessible HTML pages, with support for configured ignores.

requirements.text: The system MUST preserve standard Markdown formatting and structure in the generated HTML (e.g., headings, lists, emphasis, links, code blocks).
requirements.rationale: A stated goal is to preserve Markdown formatting and structure in the generated site and to process standard Markdown syntax.

requirements.text: The system MUST provide a command-line build workflow that generates the site output directory from the input notes.
requirements.rationale: An assumption is that a CLI build workflow is acceptable, and a success metric is that the build completes successfully.

requirements.text: The generated site MUST include client-side full-text search across note titles and body content without requiring any server requests to execute searches.
requirements.rationale: Goals and assumptions call for full-text search implemented client-side to keep the site fully static.

requirements.text: The build process MUST produce a search index artifact that is shipped with the static site and used by the client-side search feature.
requirements.rationale: To enable static, client-side full-text search, a prebuilt index must be generated and included in the output.

requirements.text: The system MUST detect internal links between notes and render them as navigable links in the generated HTML when the link target resolves to a note in the input set.
requirements.rationale: A key goal is to detect and render internal links between notes to support navigation.

requirements.text: For each note, the generated page MUST include a backlinks section listing all other notes that link to it, and each backlink entry MUST link to the source note page.
requirements.rationale: A stated goal and success metric require backlinks ("linked from") sections with clickable links.

requirements.text: The system MUST support tag extraction from notes based on at least one configurable tagging convention and expose tags per note in the generated page.
requirements.rationale: A stated goal is to support tags for browsing/filtering; tag conventions are an explicit open question and should be configurable.

requirements.text: The generated site MUST include a tags index page and per-tag pages that list all notes associated with the selected tag.
requirements.rationale: A success metric requires tag index pages where selecting a tag shows all notes containing that tag.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD provide configurable rules for internal link parsing to support one or more link syntaxes (e.g., standard Markdown links and/or wiki-style links) as selected by the user.
requirements.rationale: Linking conventions are a blocking open question; configurability reduces risk and supports different note ecosystems.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD provide configurable tag normalization rules (e.g., case handling and whitespace handling) applied consistently across tag pages and note tag displays.
requirements.rationale: Tag parsing and normalization rules are a blocking open question; consistent normalization is necessary for predictable browsing.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD generate a global navigation entry point that allows users to reach (a) an all-notes listing and (b) the tags index from any note page.
requirements.rationale: The problem statement calls for discoverability and navigability; information architecture needs include common navigational pages.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD emit build-time warnings for unresolved internal links (links whose targets do not resolve to an input note) and render them in a clearly non-navigable manner in the output.
requirements.rationale: Handling broken links is an open question; warnings improve usability while keeping output static and predictable.

requirements.text: The system COULD support incremental builds and/or a watch mode that rebuilds the site output when Markdown files change.
requirements.rationale: Incremental rebuild and watch mode are non-blocking open questions that can improve local authoring workflow.
